key_insight: A two-level machine-learning workflow can efficiently map phase stability across complex hybrid perovskite alloy compositions and reveals that Sn-based alloys are less stable than Pb-based ones.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a practical design map for tuning composition in perovskite solar cells, helping engineers target stable, high-iodine formulations while avoiding unstable regions.
method: Graph neural network interatomic potentials trained on DFT data for fast structure relaxation.
Secondary ML models to predict energies directly from unrelaxed alloy structures.
Free-energy landscape calculations across compositions, phases, disorder, and FA orientations.
evidence_signal: The models were used to compute free-energy landscapes for (Cs/FA)Pb(Br/I)3 and (Cs/FA)Sn(Br/I)3, showing narrow stable regions for Sn-based alloys and no stabilization near the center of composition space.
watch_item: The approach is computationally powerful but still depends on the quality and coverage of the DFT training data and may require careful validation when transferred to new perovskite chemistries.
paper_title: Charting the thermodynamic stability of hybrid perovskite alloys with machine learning
